results.summary_before: This design generates a 640x480 VGA video signal showing a rocket animation. It uses a standard VGA sync generator with 800 pixels per line and 525 lines per frame, producing a 59.94 Hz refresh rate at a 25.175 MHz pixel clock. The project requires a VGA Pmod connected to a monitor that supports 640x480 @ 59.94 Hz. The demo is not interactive; the user simply waits to see if the animation appears.

results.summary_before: This design uses AND gates connected to inputs 2, 3, 4, and 8 to produce an output that displays the letter 'S' on a seven-segment display when the correct password (all ones) is entered. It is tested by setting the inputs and checking the output against a truth table. External hardware includes a 7-segment display, clock, and reset. The project is a simple password-based display exercise built in Wokwi.
results.summary: This design connects AND gates to inputs 2, 3, 4, and 8, producing an output that becomes 1 only when all four inputs are 1. It is tested by setting the inputs and checking the output against the provided truth table. External hardware includes a 7-segment display, clock, and reset. The project is a simple Wokwi exercise in which the correct password (all ones) is meant to show an 'S' on the display.

results.summary_before: This is a mini two-player Bomberman game implemented in SystemVerilog, where each player has up, down, left, right and bomb buttons. The game is displayed through a VGA interface using the standard Tiny Tapeout VGA pinout. Testing consists of connecting it to a VGA monitor and using the ten buttons. It requires a VGA Pmod, buttons, wires, resistors and a breadboard, and the documentation is otherwise very brief.

results.summary_before: This project presents a small riddle where the user must enter the correct three digits on the DIP switches to display the letters 't4m' on a 7-segment display. The design uses three input pins (SC1, SC3, SC7) and seven output pins (RX0, RX1, RX3, RX4, RX5, RX6, RX7) to drive the display. It requires no external hardware beyond the development board. The design is notable for its puzzle-like interaction.

results.summary_before: This design measures the frequency of an external signal by counting pulses over 100 ms periods and displays the result on a 128x32 SSD1306 OLED display using an emulated 7-segment format. It requires an external 1 MHz clock, a PMOD OLED display, and the signal to be measured connected to the input pin. The design is implemented in SystemVerilog and uses SPI to communicate with the OLED. No silicon test results are provided, so the actual performance is not documented.
